name: Waiping
description: A star 95 parsecs away, 35 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 3786: radius 34.829 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 290.624 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.065) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 3786: effective temperature 4041 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.074)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 3786: distance 95.42 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.021), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 95 parsecs away, 35 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 291 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,041 K, so 34.829 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 3786: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Delta Piscium
quotes.card: Delta Piscium, also named Waiping, is a solitary, orange-hued star in the zodiac constellation of Pisces.
quotes.introduction: It has an apparent visual magnitude of +4.4, so it is bright enough to be faintly visible to the naked eye.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 2556759229189045632 (quality A), from 2008AJ....135..209M; Gaia DR3 measures none
